subject: Throughput & SLO follow-up (tokens/sec, QPS, peak vs steady)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@fintechx.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 16:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: throughput and SLO numbers (recap + ask)

Alex — thanks for the call earlier. Quick written recap so we have the numbers in one place and clear next steps. I captured the items Jonas and Dev asked us to confirm for sizing the inference footprint and confirming we can meet your SLOs.

Summary (from today's call)
- Goal SLOs: p95 end-to-end response time target: 350ms for non-streamed responses, and TTFB (first token) <= 250ms for streamed responses.
- Steady state traffic: 40 QPS (average), average response size ~32 tokens.
- Burst/peak profile: up to 100 QPS sustained for short windows (~20–45 minutes) around market opens.
- Heavy outliers: ~5% of requests are long-form (>= 120 tokens); median response length ~28 tokens.
- Concurrency: baseline concurrent requests observed: ~60; expected peak concurrency: ~220.
- Streaming: front-end requires token-by-token streaming for progressive render; cannot wait for full response for those flows.

Key numbers for sizing (from our notes)
- Steady-state token throughput: 40 QPS * 32 tokens = ~1280 tokens/sec.
- Peak token throughput: 100 QPS * 32 tokens = ~3200 tokens/sec (not including long-form outliers).
- Worst-case token throughput accounting for 5% long responses: add ~ (0.05 * 92 extra tokens * 100 QPS) ≈ 460 tokens/sec during peaks (est).

Open asks for you (to confirm)
1) Can you send a small sample of production traffic (anonymized) or a histogram of response-token lengths? That will help us tune batching windows.
2) Are all routes streaming, or only a subset (search/assist routes vs batch summarization)?
3) Typical prompt + context length distribution (avg and 95th). Do you expect conversation state to blow past 2k tokens often?

Attachments: fintechx_requirement_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet with routes & traffic split)

Next steps (proposed)
- We’ll run a preliminary sizing estimate and provide two options: (1) Hosted autoscaling baseline with recommended config to hit p95 targets; (2) Dedicated reserved pool (monthly commit) with estimated GPUs to meet peak with headroom.
- Engineering deep-dive: schedule 60-minute session next week to review traces and tokenization specifics (Jonas + Dev).
- I’ll attach a first-pass latency/SLA note by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks — Marissa

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Response token distribution: avg ~28 tokens; 95th ~120 tokens; 99th ~260 tokens (these are user-visible responses, system prompts excluded). I attached the per-route histogram to the spreadsheet.
- Streaming requirement: only the primary assist route (web UI/live chat) needs token-level streaming with TTFB <= 200ms ideally. Background summarization and batch jobs can be non-streamed.
- Conversation length: most sessions stay under 2k tokens; around 7% of active sessions exceed that during extended workflows.
- Concurrency nuance: our active-user concurrency is ~8–12 sessions per user, but the total across all instances averages 60 concurrent requests and spikes to ~220 during market events.

I uploaded a traffic sample to the Drive link in the sheet. Let me know if you need the tokenized form or raw JSON.

Appreciate the histograms and the Drive upload — that helps a lot. Based on the clarified distribution, Jonas and I sketched two initial sizing options for a PoC (high-level, ballpark):

Option A — Hosted (autoscaled, production but with burst headroom):
- Target: meet streaming TTFB <= 200–250ms p95 for primary route while autoscaling to peak.
- Recommended baseline: instance pool equivalent to ~4 x A100-class GPUs for steady-state traffic (40 QPS, 1280 tokens/sec).
- Burst capacity: autoscale up to ~12 GPU equivalents to comfortably hit peak token throughput ~3200–4000 tokens/sec (accounting for long outliers).
- Config: short batching windows for streaming routes (5–15ms), dynamic KV caching for repeated prefixes, and per-route batching limits.
- Expected p95: ~200–350ms depending on quantization and kernel selection; we’ll refine after trace analysis.

Option B — Dedicated reserved (predictable latency & cost):
- Target: fixed pool sized for 95th peak with 15–20% headroom for bursts.
- Recommended sizing: 8 x A100-class GPUs reserved, with burstable pool (ephemeral) to scale to 12–14 for extreme events.
- Advantages: more control over kernel selection, lower tail latency variability, and predictable unit costs.

Notes from engineering (Jonas/Dev):
- Streaming TTFB is most sensitive to batching windows and kernel warmness. If we can warm model kernels on predictable diurnal patterns, p95 improves significantly.
- Tokenization: need the tokenized traces to compute batch size optima.

Next steps
1) Engineering deep-dive: Jonas + Dev to review the Drive sample on Friday 3/20 at 10am PT (I’ll send the invite).
2) We’ll send a short one-page SLO/latency estimate (pdf) and a cost ballpark for both options by EOD Monday 3/22.
3) Please confirm which routes require streaming and share tokenized traces if possible.

Attaching: redwood_latencies_and_sla.pdf (first-pass SLO note)
